html:
The Keyauwee were a small Siouan-speaking people of the Piedmont of North Carolina, in today's Randolph County near High Point. Their village was surrounded by a palisade and cornfields.

The English explorer John Lawson visited them in 1701 and described them in his book about Carolina. Soon after, under pressure from war and disease, they moved east and south, and joined other small peoples. By the mid 1700s they had merged with the Catawba and others. Neighbours: Saura and Occaneechi.
